note: Venture packages (EE-067): what a founder walks away with. A package is a set of records that together serve one receiver (the founder, investors, a cofounder, engineering, partners, counsel, the team), complete when every required record is confirmed by a person, at which point it is ready to hand off, to a person or to an agent. Which packages a venture needs depends on its phase and on its situation, so each package has a prior per phase, raised or lowered by facts, in the same form as need-now (EE-028). Facts come from the venture's records first; the question matrix asks a reasoning model (Jev, or the founder's own agent) only what the records do not say, and leaves what it cannot answer to the founder. Agents never come in a package: an agent that works a package is a package enhancement. Version 0.x: ours and unevaluated.

foundation.title: Strategic foundation
foundation.for: the founder, and anyone who joins
foundation.purpose: What the venture is, why, for whom and with what: the records every other package draws on.
foundation.why: Every venture needs it, in every phase; it is what the founder reviews near daily

validation.title: Validation
validation.purpose: Whether the problem is real, whether this solves it, whether people pay and keep using it, with the evidence graded.
validation.why: The work of Discovery and Validation; it fades once retention holds

marketing.title: Marketing
marketing.for: engineering, who builds the site from it
marketing.purpose: Who the site speaks to, what goes where and why, and the public variants to publish: the business side's handoff to engineering (EE-065).
marketing.why: Once there is something to show, or a site already speaks for the venture

investor.title: Investor
investor.purpose: The case for the venture: problem, solution, market, team, where it is going, and what an investor would own.
investor.why: Only while raising, or when the venture means to take outside money

team.title: Cofounder and team
team.purpose: Who the venture needs, what each person brings, who decides what, and on what terms people join.
team.why: When the founder is looking for a cofounder, has one, or is hiring

partner.title: Partner
partner.for: the partners a product is offered to
partner.purpose: What the venture offers partners, what they get and give, and whom it serves through them (B2B2C).
partner.why: Only when the product is offered to partners who serve customers of their own

governance.title: Ownership and governance
governance.purpose: Who owns what, who decides what, what may be published, and how the venture ends.
governance.why: Once ownership is shared, outside money comes in, or the field is regulated

operations.title: Operations
operations.for: the team that runs the venture day to day
operations.purpose: The departments, who hands what to whom, and whether the venture is ready to run without the founder in every loop.
operations.why: Once more than a couple of people, or a service delivered by people, has to run

enhancements.agents: An agent that works a package (drafts its records, keeps them current, acts on them) is a package enhancement. Naive's packages hold records only; Mentura and the founder's own agents enhance them. The hackathon demo includes routing and the harness agent's passes to show the enhancement.

questions.note: The question matrix: what a reasoning model answers about a venture to decide which packages fit it now. Each question sets one fact. A question is asked only in the phases it lists and only when the venture's records do not already settle the fact (from: records). Jev answers each as a typed noul question over the venture's records; an answer at or above 0.7 sets the fact, at or below 0.3 clears it, and anything between stays open for the founder.

items.ask: Is the venture raising money from investors now, or about to?
Does the venture have a public website, or plan one within the next month?
items.from: a site presence record (a site Naive has read)

items.ask: Is the product offered to partners or intermediaries who serve customers of their own?
Will the venture hire anyone, or bring on a cofounder, in the next three months?
items.from: the founder's flags (hiring) and the team decision

items.ask: Does the venture work in a regulated field (health, finance, education, legal, children, public sector)?
Does the founder mean to sell the venture or take it public one day?
